title: introduce page-admission-gate-and-micro-reclaim-window-to-kv-cache
author: Aisha Moreno
description: Motivation: Reduce tail latency and memory churn from aggressive concurrent reclamation in the KV cache while keeping peak residency high for hot prefixes. This PR adds a lightweight page-admission gate that defers admitting cold pages into active residency when memory pressure is transient, and a micro-reclaim window that consolidates small reclamation events into a single in-place reclaim to reduce fragmentation and CPU scheduling overhead. Design: 1) Page admission gate: a short-lifetime admission token is issued per tenant/prefix and is consumed by cold-promote operations. When token budget is exhausted, subsequent cold pages are redirected to a transient spill buffer (on-disk spill file or separate page pool) until tokens refill; tokens refill at a kernel-configurable rate driven by memory-pressure signals. 2) Micro-reclaim window: reclamation work is coalesced for up to Nms (configurable) so that many small object frees are applied together; the implementation uses a per-shard reclaim queue and a timer-driven coalescer that runs reclaim inline to keep hot-path jitter bounded. 3) Batch-awareness hooks: the admission gate exposes a hint to the continuous-batcher so that long-running batched requests avoid promoting ephemeral prefixes until admission stabilizes. 4) Telemetry: fragmentation heatmap counters, admission token burn rate, micro-reclaim coalesce ratio, and transient spill bytes are added to the memory telemetry pipeline and the Console dashboards. Implementation: changes touch src/kv/cache_manager.cpp (admission token bookkeeping, transient spill glue), src/kv/reclaimer.cpp (per-shard reclaim queue and coalescer), src/scheduler/batcher.cpp (hint propagation), src/runtime/kernel_selector.cpp (tuning knob for coalesce timing), tests/perf/kv_memory_pressure_bench.cc (microbench scenarios), docs/ops/kv-tuning.md (operational guidance), and an e2e smoke fixture under infra/test-fixtures/kv_admission_smoke.yaml for Private installs. Backwards compatibility: default knobs preserve current behavior (admission tokens unlimited, coalesce window = 0) so this is opt-in via feature flags or config. Testing: unit coverage for token lifecycle and reclaim coalescer, integration runs on perf-canary with 72-hour soak demonstrating ~18% decrease in 95th-percentile eviction latency on synthetic mix A and ~6% reduction in fragmentation score for multi-tenant workloads, transient spill enabled only in low-memory transient scenarios. Rollout plan: gated behind feature-flag + gradual rollout to Dedicated then Hosted with telemetry checks and automatic rollback on >5% increase in median latency. This PR also includes an operations doc with recommended token rates by tenant size and a simple script to backfill transient spill files during node maintenance.
commits: Initial implementation of admission token ledger and transient spill pool
Add per-shard reclaim queue and timer coalescer
Expose batch-awareness hint to continuous batcher
Add telemetry emitters and dashboard wiring
Fix race in reclaim queue pop under stress
release_notes: Introduce optional page admission gate to reduce transient promotion of cold pages; add micro-reclaim window to coalesce small frees and reduce fragmentation and CPU churn. Defaults are off to preserve current behavior.
review_comments: Marcus Chen: Can we avoid extra allocation for the transient spill pool on hosts that do not enable disk spill? Suggest lazily initializing the spill file resource.
Author(Aisha Moreno): Spill pool is lazily opened; added a patch to ensure no fd is consumed unless a transient spill is triggered (see commit 4).
Priya Kapoor: Need clearer guidance on token-rate defaults for small Dedicated instances — the ops doc has a heuristic but prefer concrete numbers for 16GB/32GB/64GB configs.
Author: Added recommended token rates and a script to calculate tenant-specific rates based on steady-state working set (see docs/ops/kv-tuning.md and tools/ops/backfill_transient_spill.py).
Liam O'Neill: In the reclaim coalescer, under heavy concurrency we saw a rare assertion; added a fix to use try_lock and fallback to immediate reclaim if coalescer is contended.
CI: perf-canary run showed 18% p95 eviction latency reduction on synthetic mix A and no regression on mix B. Re-run on dedicated-staging after race fix passed.
